locator: I q.3 a.1 co., second proof: Ostensum est autem supra quod Deus est primum ens
interpretation: Aquinas' back-reference to q.2 a.3, read as being about the prima via's first mover moved by none (as the first proof of the same article reads 'Deus' as 'primum movens immobile'). The pinned prima via text does not state it, and result AQUINAS-ST-I-Q3-A1-FIRST-MOVER-PURE-ACT verifies (firstWayDoesNotYieldPureAct) that the prima via premises do not entail pure act without it. A defensible alternative reading refers the back-reference to the fourth way (maxime ens), which would make applying it to the first mover a further identification. Open premise on the root path.
